newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy fund flows benefit from interest rate falls.
newsitem.headline: Italy fund flows benefit from interest rate falls.

text.p: Cash flows into Italian investment funds are benefitting from the fall in official interest rates, while stategists say Italian equities are now at very attractive levels compared with other investments opportunities.

Data released by investment fund body Assogestioni showed Italian invesment funds had a net inflow of 9.331 trillion lire in November from a 7.940 trillion lire inflow in October. Within the overall figure, the inflow into bonds rose, while outflows from equities were cut to 216 billion from 925 billion lire.

"The fall in outflows from equity funds is a consequence of interest rates coming down, and with equities at very attractive levels one can envisage a switch out of bonds into shares," said one head of equity sales at an Italian broker.

Flows into bond funds have gained as the market rallied sharply this autumn on the back of a deficit-cutting budget and the run-up to the lira's entry into Europe's ERM, but as prices have risen bond yields have fallen and investors are likely to search around for better value, dealers said.
"Investors are beginning to consider that a switch into equities and out of bonds might be a good move, but this has not happened yet," said one equity strategist at an Italian bank.

Italian equity funds, like overall equity funds, have shown a sharp fall in outflows to 28 billion lire in November from a 159 billion lire outflow in October, but strategists say the outlook for equities depends on the international funds.

Official Italian interest rates have come down twice in the last five months, with the Bank of Italy cutting 75 basis points of the discount rate both in July and October to bring it down to 7.5 percent. Economists still hope for a further rate fall before the end of 1996 as inflation continues to slide lower.

The Milan stock market traditionally shows a rally at the end of the year up to Christmas and into the New Year, and some strategists believe many funds could be attracted into investing in Italian equities in this period.
